To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the laser induced infrared spectral shift is a new phenomenon in the MgB2 superconducting films.

(i) the spectral shift of the absorption bands is observed for the MgB2 superconductors, (ii) the spectral shift is in opposite directions for the 1.54 μm and 10.6 μm lasers, (iii) the spectral shift correlates well with the shift of the critical temperature.
the spectral shift of the IR absorption maxima in the vicinity of ~20cm(-1) is a direct manifestation of the laser induced change of the superconducting state of MgB2: Cr2O3 films.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the laser-induced infrared spectral shift of MgB2:Ch superconductor films, which is a promising material for high-temperature superconducting applications.
the photoinduced changes of the MgB(2):Cr superconductor.

the laser induced infrared spectral shift, the photoinduced charge redistribution, the kinetics of the photovoltage response and the time kinetics in the vicinity of the superconducting transition temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spectral shift of the IR absorption bands of the superconducting MgB2: Cr2O3 films under the action of laser illumination was established.
the spectral shift of the critical temperature of the MgB(2):Cr superconductor can be controlled and modified by laser illumination.
the observed spectral shifts are due to the charge density redistribution in the superconductor films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spectral shift of the IR max is a consequence of the charge transfer processes between the dopant and the MgB2 lattice and it is a result of the laser induced redistribution of the charge density.
the photoinduced spectral shift of the IR spectra is due to the change of charge density redistribution in the MgB2 crystal.
the photoinduced spectral shifts of the superconducting MgB2: Cr2O3 films are related to the photoinduced charge redistribution in the vicinity of the Cr atoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the laser irradiation can be used for tuning the properties of the superconductor.

the photoresponse kinetics of the MgB(2):Cr2O(3) films is a complex process, and the photoinduced changes of the charge distribution in the films are not instantaneous, but rather a time dependent process.
the laser irradiation can be used to tune superconducting properties of MgB2.
